ai.title: GLM referral banner persists across session states
ai.summary: Referral data persists in landing view via new process-wide cache in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-referral-cache.ts`. Server omits referral blocks after join/end states, causing banner disappearance during `ended` row sweep; `rememberReferral` captures last valid block, `getCachedReferral` restores it in `toLandingSession`. Scope covers `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` integration and `cli/src/components/freebuff-referral-banner.tsx` UI updates. Streak dots logic in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts` changed from rolling modulo to `Math.min` cap, keeping 7+ day streaks visually full.

eli5.text: If you use the CodeBuff assistant in the terminal and click over to the GLM referral banner, that banner will now stick around after your session ends or while you are in the queue, instead of vanishing during the brief moment the app returns to the landing screen. The app now remembers the last referral it showed you and re-displays it on the landing view until a fresh, clean response comes back, so the banner no longer blinks out during the join end, and return-to-landing transition. The 'sessions left' text in that same banner also got a color fix so it reads correctly against the green button, and the streak line in the waiting room now stays visually full once you hit a seven-day streak rather than resetting its look.

facts: On the landing screen the streak rides on the heading row, right-aligned. Below ~50 cols the heading + dots get squashed together, so drop the streak to its own line under the heading instead.
"●●○○○○○". Fills to "●●●●●●●" at 7, then gains a trailing "+" ("●●●●●●●+") for any streak beyond the week so long runs read as "earned and still going" rather than just maxed out.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant in a terminal window that's narrower than about 50 characters, the daily streak counter now moves below the heading instead of squeezing against it. The referral message on the landing screen no longer mentions a fixed friend cap, so the wording stays accurate whether or not that limit changes later.

ai.title: skill handler reads disk-first
ai.summary: Skill handler now reads from disk first, falling back to session cache. Ensures skills installed or updated via `npx skills add` reflect latest contents immediately. Affects `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/skill.ts` and `common/src/tools/params/tool/skill.ts`. Base agent prompt updated to guide users through community skill discovery and installation.

eli5.text: When you load a skill by name, your assistant now always grabs the latest copy it finds on your computer instead of relying on a version it remembered when your session started. This means if you just installed or updated a skill (for example by running a command in your terminal), that new version is used right away rather than the old one it had cached. You would not see anything different unless you had updated a skill during the current session, in which case the changes show up immediately instead of on your next session.

ai.title: Add ipinfo ASN type benign and hosting checks
ai.summary: Added `isFreebuffBenignAsType` and `isFreebuffHostingAsType` helpers to `common/src/util/freebuff-privacy.ts`. These functions classify ipinfo's `as.type` field to distinguish benign networks (ISP, business, education, government) from hosting infrastructure, which is the only meaningful abuse signal. The change ensures real users behind ordinary networks are not incorrectly flagged by hosting heuristics.

eli5.text: When the service checks whether an internet address belongs to a regular person or to a shady server farm, it now listens to a label that the address database already provides. Real users sitting behind home internet, business fiber, school networks, or government lines are no longer bumped by hosting-only filters. The result, live today: fewer honest visitors get mistaken for VPN or bot traffic because the system finally trusts the ordinary-network tag.
